name: Amazon Leo (Project Kuiper production satellite)
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'Amazon Leo' type. Body frame: +Z nadir, +X velocity. A 2 m bus, a partly mirrored nadir antenna panel, and one solar panel standing up from the bus (long axis near local vertical) that turns about that axis to face the Sun. Benchmark: mallama2026_amazon_leo (6.81 at 1000 km, operational mode, 630 km). The layout follows the authors' interpretation of Amazon's images (their Figure 4).

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: 2 x 2 x 1.2 m bus, nadir-pointing along velocity
sources.source: Gunter's Space Page, 'Kuiper / Amazon LEO': about 2 m long and in diameter, 10 m span; ~550-600 kg (height 1.2 m: estimate).

sources.subject: nadir_antenna_panel
sources.value: 3 x 2 m nadir panel (three deployed antenna panels)
sources.source: Mallama, Cole, Respler & Harrington 2026 (arXiv:2601.07708) section 4 and Figure 4: 'three antenna panels are folded at launch and deploy to form a large, nadir-facing panel, at least part of which is mirror-faced', 'the solar panel can rotate around its long axis to track the Sun', seen 'oriented close to the local vertical'. Size estimated from the 2 m bus (three 1 x 2 m panels).

sources.subject: solar_panel
sources.value: one 8 x 2 m panel, long axis to zenith (10 m span with the bus)
sources.source: Mallama, Cole, Respler & Harrington 2026 (arXiv:2601.07708) section 4 and Figure 4: 'three antenna panels are folded at launch and deploy to form a large, nadir-facing panel, at least part of which is mirror-faced', 'the solar panel can rotate around its long axis to track the Sun', seen 'oriented close to the local vertical'; Gunter's Space Page, 'Kuiper / Amazon LEO': about 2 m long and in diameter, 10 m span; ~550-600 kg. Length DERIVED from the span; width estimate.

sources.subject: array
sources.value: the panel turns about its (vertical) long axis toward the Sun
sources.source: Mallama, Cole, Respler & Harrington 2026 (arXiv:2601.07708) section 4 and Figure 4: 'three antenna panels are folded at launch and deploy to form a large, nadir-facing panel, at least part of which is mirror-faced', 'the solar panel can rotate around its long axis to track the Sun', seen 'oriented close to the local vertical'.

sources.value: a gen-1-like mirror with a larger diffuse part (0.1): 'partly mirror-faced'
